sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Direct bachelor's-to-PhD eligible in principle: degree before entry, at least 18 advanced-undergraduate
mathematics credits and preparation for two basic first-year courses. No standalone incoming MA. [s1]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD; prepare advanced-course descriptions; request fee waiver from department before
paying if needed. [s1] [s3]
Adviser contact [Unresolved]
Faculty fit can be investigated before applying; no prior-supervisor agreement requirement found. Faculty list
below is a partial paper-verified shortlist, not a complete census. [s8]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Submit electronically, then use status page for reference receipt/updates, score receipt, additional materials,
final-record deadlines and accepting/declining. [s6]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
January 5 is standing annual guidance; no explicitly labeled Fall 2027 deadline found. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
Ten-month TA stipend amount not verified. Tuition waiver, health insurance and academic fees covered. Many
students receive annual Excellence Supplements of USD1,000 to over USD5,000; this is additional competitive
support, not the base stipend. [s4]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Normally at most five years, subject to progress and duties; summer positions usually available to continuing
students but not guaranteed. [s4]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International TAs are contemplated explicitly; oral-English certification required before teaching.
Scholarship-specific nationality rules need checking. [s1] [s4]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Typically GPA3.0; two qualifiers before second year and third by May of second year; English certification
before year2; adviser by end semester5, comprehensive exam by semester6; satisfactory TA work. [s4]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
No separate departmental funding form established; ask if a particular fellowship requires
nomination/additional materials. [s4]

Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Excellence Supplements, summer teaching, research grants and fellowships; availability varies. [s4]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD85 international, nonrefundable; application not reviewed without payment. Payment in application;
central page permits card or US-bank check/money order. [s5]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Request from intended program; Mathematics FAQ directs special requests to Katie Greenland
(kle16@psu.edu) or gradstudies@math.psu.edu. Eligibility and 2027 deadline not specified. [s3] [s5]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Jack Huizenga
Moduli of sheaves and bundles, interpolation, Brill-Noether theory. [s8] [s9]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2026 · Waldschmidt constants of symmetric sets of points in P3
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
John Lesieutre
Birational geometry, divisor positivity, dynamics and arithmetic degrees. [s8] [s10]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2026 · The volume of a divisor and cusp excursions of geodesics in hyperbolic manifolds
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
Number theory
Mihran Papikian
Function-field arithmetic, Drinfeld modules/modular curves and number rings. [s8] [s11]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2026 · On ideal class groups of totally degenerate number rings
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
Kirsten Eisenträger
Number theory and arithmetic geometry; algorithms for elliptic-curve endomorphism rings, supersingular
isogeny graphs, quaternion algebras, arithmetic logic and cryptography. [s8] [s12] [qbr10_q1] [qbr10_q2] [qbr10_q3]
[qbr10_q4]

Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2026 · Generating sets for maximal orders in rational quaternion algebras
With eight coauthors; submitted 7 October 2026. Generators of prescribed prime-power norm, Brandt matrices, theta bounds and
supersingular isogeny graphs.
Research evidence: 2026 · Connecting Kani's Lemma and path-finding in the Bruhat-Tits tree to compute supersingular
endomorphism rings
With Gabrielle Scullard; original 2024, revised 21 January 2026. Deterministic polynomial-time computation under explicit input
hypotheses.
Evidence history and corrections (earlier statements may be superseded)
 Earlier interests: Arithmetic geometry, algorithms and cryptography; recent paper metadata still requires verification.
